item.title: Military Proposes Shift to 3-Rank System for Soldiers After 64 Years… "Streamlining Due to Reduced Service Period" (軍, 64년 만에 병사 ‘3계급’ 체제 추진…“복무기간 단축 따른 효율화”)
item.description:
Military Proposes Shift to 3-Rank System for Soldiers After 64 Years… "Streamlining Due to Reduced Service Period" (軍, 64년 만에 병사 ‘3계급’ 체제 추진…“복무기간 단축 따른 효율화”)

<<>> The Ministry of National Defense stated on the 9th that as part of defense reforms planned through 2040, it will push to reduce the current 4-rank structure for active-duty soldiers to a 3-rank system. Additionally, the current 4-rank structure for non-commissioned officers (NCOs) will be changed to a 5-rank system. ()

Lee In-goo, the Defense Ministry's personnel planning official, made this announcement at a defense reform seminar held at the War Memorial of Korea in Yongsan-gu, Seoul, saying, "There is a need to reorganize the military rank system to enhance the efficiency of military personnel operations." The seminar was held to outline the basic direction of reforms, as the military plans to finalize a basic defense reform plan by July. (국방부가 2040년까지 추진하는 국방 개혁의 일환으로 현재 4계급 구조인 현역병 계급 체계를 3계급으로 줄이는 방안을 추진하겠다고 9일 밝혔다. 또 4계급 구조인 부사관은 5계급 체계로 바꾸기로 했다.)

The military introduced the current soldier rank system (private, private first class, corporal, sergeant) in 1962, marking the first change to the soldier rank structure in 64 years. Meanwhile, the current 4-rank structure for NCOs (sergeant, staff sergeant, sergeant first class, master sergeant) was established in 1994. (이인구 국방부 인사기획관은 이날 서울 용산구 전쟁기념관에서 열린 국방개혁 세미나에서 “군의 인력 운영 효율화를 위한 군 계급 체계 개편이 필요하다”며 이같이 말했다. 이번 세미나는 군이 오는 7월까지 국방개혁 기본계획을 마련할 예정인 가운데, 개혁의 기본 방향을 설명하기 위해 열렸다.)

Regarding the shift to a 3-rank soldier system, the Defense Ministry said it aims to "address inefficiencies resulting from maintaining a 4-rank structure even after the reduction of active-duty service periods in 2018." Based on Army standards, the service period for active-duty soldiers was cut to 1 year and 6 months, making it difficult to sustain the existing 4-rank system. (군은 지난 1962년 현재의 병 계급 체제(이등병, 일등병, 상등병, 병장)를 도입했는데, 64년 만에 병 계급 구조 변경에 나선 것이다. 부사관은 지난 1994년 현재의 4계급(하사, 중사, 상사, 원사) 체계가 완성됐다.)

However, it has not yet been determined which of the current 4 ranks will be eliminated or whether the rank names will change under the new 3-rank system. (국방부는 병 계급을 3계급으로 바꾸는 데 대해 “2018년 현역병 복무 기간 단축 후에도 4계급 체계를 유지함에 따른 비효율적 요소를 개선하기 위한 것”이라고 했다. 육군 기준, 현역병 복무 기간이 1년 6개월로 줄어들면서 기존 4계급 체제를 유지하기가 어려웠다는 것이다.)

Regarding the change to a 5-rank NCO system, the ministry stated, "It is intended to establish a system where personnel serve an appropriate period at each rank before promotion to the next," adding, "This can address issues such as prolonged stagnation at the sergeant first class rank, which can last up to 17 years, thereby increasing operational efficiency in personnel management." (다만 3계급 체계가 되면서 현 4계급 가운데 어떤 계급이 없어지는지, 계급명이 바뀌는 것인지 등은 아직 정해지지 않은 것으로 알려졌다.)

The core of this reform plan is to restructure the military on the premise of troop reduction. The Defense Ministry announced that it will redesign the defense workforce structure—including active-duty personnel, civilian workers, public-service employees, and standby reserve forces—from a total force perspective, adjusting it from the current 500,000 to around 500,000 by 2040. (또 부사관을 4계급 체계로 변경하는 데 대해선 “계급별 적정 기간 복무 후 상위 계급으로 진급하는 체계를 마련하기 위한 것”이라며 “현재 상사 계급의 장기 정체가 최대 17년에 이르는 등 문제를 해소함으로써 인력 운영의 효율성을 증대할 수 있다”고 말했다.)

Reforms to the conscription system were also foreshadowed. The ministry stated it would maintain the universal conscription system but consider selective volunteer enlistment, along with developing the rank system, adjusting service periods, improving the efficiency of the defense recruitment system, and reducing or abolishing the alternative service system. Selective volunteer enlistment is interpreted not as a shift to an all-volunteer force, but as combining conscription with volunteer recruitment in some areas while maintaining the framework of the draft. (이번 개혁안의 핵심은 병력 감소를 전제로 군 구조를 다시 짜겠다는 것이다. 국방부는 현역과 군무원, 공무직 근로자, 상비예비군 등을 포함한 국방인력 구조를 총 전력 차원에서 재설계해 현 50만명 규모에서 2040년까지 50만명 수준으로 조정하겠다고 밝혔다.)

The Defense Ministry plans to compensate for the power gaps from troop reductions with artificial intelligence (AI) and unmanned systems. The final state of the 2040 military structure was presented as a "troop-reduced military structure augmented by AI-based manned-unmanned combined combat systems." (병역제도 개편도 예고됐다. 국방부는 국민개병제를 기반으로 하되 선택적 모병제를 검토하고, 계급 체계 발전과 복무 기간 조정, 국방 모집 체계 효율화, 보충역 제도 감축 및 폐지 등을 추진하겠다고 밝혔다. 선택적 모병제는 전면 모병제로 전환하는 것이 아니라 징병제 틀을 유지하면서 일부 분야에 모병 방식을 결합하는 방안으로 해석된다.)

Accordingly, units operating manned-unmanned combined combat systems, such as drones and robots, will be significantly expanded across all branches. Drone forces will be scaled up to about 30 times their current size, and capabilities in space, cyber, and electromagnetic domains will also be strengthened. Guard posts (GOP), general outposts (GP), naval bases, military airfields, and key military facilities will be converted to AI-based surveillance systems. The ministry explained this will reduce border troops while improving the quality of surveillance. The coastal guard mission will also be considered for transfer to the Coast Guard, following consultations with relevant ministries. (국방부는 병력 감축에 따른 전력 공백을 인공지능(AI)과 무인 체계로 보완한다는 계획이다. 2040년 군 구조의 최종 상태로는 ‘AI 기반 유·무인 복합 전투 체계로 증강한 병력 절감형 군 구조’를 제시했다.)

Reserve forces will also be overhauled. The Defense Ministry announced it will expand the standby reserve force to 50,000 personnel by 2040 and enhance the weapon systems and equipment of mobilization-oriented units, such as mobilization divisions, to the level of active-duty divisions. Integrating regional reserve organizations into the national military structure is also under consideration. (이에 따라 드론과 로봇 등 유·무인 복합 전투 체계를 운용하는 부대를 전군에 대폭 확대한다. 드론 전력은 현재의 약 30배 규모로 늘리고, 우주·사이버·전자기 영역 능력도 강화하기로 했다. GOP와 GP, 군항, 군 비행장, 군 중요 시설 등은 AI 기반 경계 작전 체계로 전환한다. 국방부는 이를 통해 경계 병력을 줄이면서도 경계의 질을 높일 수 있다고 설명했다. 해안경계 임무는 관련 부처 협의를 거쳐 해양경찰로 전환하는 방안도 추진한다.)

In the advanced technology sector, the ministry will pursue a major AI transformation in defense, integrated data utilization, building defense AI infrastructure, and establishing ultra-fast, hyper-connected networks. The Defense Ministry also plans to "train 500,000 drone warriors" to expand the drone operation capabilities of soldiers and reservists. (예비전력도 손본다. 국방부는 상비예비군을 2040년까지 5만명 규모로 확대하고, 동원사단 등 동원위주부대의 무기체계와 장비를 상비사단 수준으로 보강하겠다고 밝혔다. 지역예비군 조직을 국군 조직으로 통합하는 방안도 검토 대상에 포함됐다.)

The Defense Ministry will incorporate opinions from the seminar and finalize the basic defense reform plan by July. (첨단기술 분야에서는 국방 AI 대전환, 데이터 통합 활용, 국방 AI 인프라 구축, 초고속·초연결 네트워크 구축 등을 추진한다. 국방부는 ‘50만 드론전사 양성’도 추진해 장병과 예비군의 드론 운용 능력을 확대하겠다고 했다.)

item.title: President Lee Embarks on 10-Day European Tour for Series of Summits, Attending G7 for Second Consecutive Year (李대통령, 유럽 순방 열흘간 연쇄 정상회담… G7도 2년 연속 참석)
item.description:
President Lee Embarks on 10-Day European Tour for Series of Summits, Attending G7 for Second Consecutive Year (李대통령, 유럽 순방 열흘간 연쇄 정상회담… G7도 2년 연속 참석)

President Lee Jae-myung departed for a European tour on the 9th via Seoul Airport in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, on the occasion of attending the G7 summit. The president will visit Belgium, Italy, Vatican City, and France over 10 days and 8 nights. This marks his first European tour since taking office, and he will attend the G7 summit for the second consecutive year. (이재명 대통령이 G7 정상회의 참석을 계기로 9일 경기도 성남시 서울공항을 통해 유럽 순방길에 올랐다. 이 대통령은 8박 10일 동안 벨기에·이탈리아·바티칸·프랑스를 방문한다. 유럽 순방은 이 대통령 취임 뒤 처음이다. G7 정상회의엔 2년 연속 참석한다.)

On the first day, the 9th (local time), President Lee arrived in Brussels, Belgium, in the afternoon and began his tour schedule with a dinner meeting with overseas Koreans. Before departing, the president posted on X (formerly Twitter) about his first destination, Belgium, stating, "As a logistics hub of Europe with an innovative ecosystem for small and medium-sized enterprise growth, it will be a solid partner in expanding companies' entry into Europe and creating new growth opportunities." This year marks the 125th anniversary of diplomatic relations between South Korea and Belgium. (이 대통령은 첫날인 9일(현지 시각) 오후 벨기에 브뤼셀에 도착해 동포 만찬 간담회로 순방 일정을 시작했다. 이 대통령은 출국 전 X(엑스·옛 트위터)에 첫 방문지인 벨기에를 두고 “유럽의 물류 중심이자 혁신적인 중소기업 성장 생태계를 갖췄다”며 “기업들의 유럽 진출을 확대하고 새 성장 기회를 만들어가는 든든한 파트너가 될 것”이라고 밝혔다. 올해는 한·벨기에 수교 125주년이다.)

On the 10th, the president will hold a summit with Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever and meet with King Philippe in the afternoon. He will also hold summits with European Council President António Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on the same day. The summit with Belgium is expected to cover enhancing bilateral trade and expanding cooperation with small and medium-sized enterprises. Economic exchanges are also anticipated to dominate discussions in the meeting with the EU. (10일에는 바르트 더 베버르 벨기에 총리와 정상회담을, 오후에는 필립 국왕과 면담한다. 같은 날 안토니우 코스타 유럽연합(EU) 정상회의 상임의장, 우르줄라 폰데어라이엔 EU 집행위원장과의 정상회담도 소화한다. 벨기에와의 정상회담에서는 양국 무역 증진과 중소기업 협력 확대가 논의 테이블에 오를 것으로 예상된다. EU와의 회담에서도 경제 교류가 논의의 주를 이룰 전망이다.)

From the 11th to the 13th, the president will visit Italy, following an invitation from Italian President Sergio Mattarella for a state visit. During this time, President Lee will hold a summit with President Mattarella and also meet with Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. He will also have meetings with the speakers of the Italian Senate and Chamber of Deputies. Notably, a "Korea-Italy Business Round Table" is scheduled, facilitating exchanges between companies from both countries. (11~13일에는 이탈리아를 방문한다. 세르지오 마타렐라 이탈리아 대통령의 초청에 따른 국빈 방문 일정이다. 이 대통령은 이탈리아에서 마타렐라 대통령과 정상회담을 갖고, 조르자 멜로니 국무총리와도 회담한다. 또 이탈리아 상·하원 의장과의 면담도 진행한다. 특히 이탈리아에서는 ‘한-이탈리아 비즈니스 라운드 테이블’도 열리는 등 양국 기업 간 교류도 이뤄질 예정이다.)

After the state visit to Italy, the president will visit Vatican City from the 14th to the 15th. On the 14th, President Lee will meet with Pope Leo XIV and attend a "Special Mass for Peace and Solidarity" held at the Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls. In this setting, the president is expected to express his commitment to peace on the Korean Peninsula and appeal for the support of the international community. (이탈리아 국빈 방문 이후 14~15일에는 바티칸을 방문한다. 이 대통령은 14일 레오 14세 교황과 면담하고, 성 밖 성 바오로 성당에서 열리는 ‘평화와 연대를 위한 특별 미사’에 참석한다. 이 대통령은 이 자리에서 한반도 평화에 대한 의지를 표명하고 이에 대한 국제사회의 지지를 호소할 것으로 보인다.)

On the 16th, President Lee will travel to Évian, France, to participate in the G7 summit. The themes of this year's G7 summit include alleviating global imbalances and issues related to AI (artificial intelligence) and digital technology. A key point of interest is whether a summit with U.S. President Donald Trump will materialize during this G7 meeting. (이 대통령은 16일 프랑스 에비앙으로 이동해 G7 정상회의에 참석한다. 이번 G7 정상회의 주제는 글로벌 불균형 완화와 AI(인공지능)·디지털 문제 등이다. 특히 이번 G7 정상회의에서는 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령과의 정상회담 성사 여부도 관건이다.)

item.title: Give and Take... (주거니 받거니…)
item.description:
Give and Take... (주거니 받거니…)

On the 9th, the Democratic Party of Korea stated regarding its push for a "Special Counsel for Fabricated Indictments"—aimed at allowing the dismissal of charges in the case of President Lee Jae-myung—that it is "about rectifying wrongful targeted investigations." After President Lee remarked the previous day on the dismissal of charges, saying, "If something is wrong, it can be corrected," the party effectively announced its intention to re-pursue the special counsel law. The party had previously shelved the special counsel law after encountering opposition while trying to push it through before the local elections. The opposition party countered, calling it a "self-granted pardon." <<> Democratic Party Spokesperson Jang Yoon-mi said at a briefing that day regarding the special counsel for fabricated indictments: "The core is to use an investigation to uncover the prosecution's unreasonable targeted investigations and allegations of testimony coercion, which cannot be explained without removing the three letters of 'Lee Jae-myung.'" She added, "Is it a violation of the rule of law to correct wrongful targeted investigations, or is it a violation of the rule of law to cover up and neglect past wrongful investigations? No politician should ever become the target of a targeted investigation like President Lee Jae-myung was." <<> President Lee, during a press conference the previous day marking his first anniversary in office, said regarding the possibility of dismissing charges in his own trial, "If I give my conclusion, it should be done according to the law and common sense," adding, "If it is revealed to be a fabricated indictment, there is no choice but to proceed." He then lent support to the Democratic Party's push for the special counsel law, saying, "From the perspective of the people or the opposition party, wouldn't it be better to have a neutral special counsel?" The scope of the special counsel investigation includes eight cases related to the president, such as allegations of corruption in the development of Daejang-dong and Baekhyeon-dong. <<> Democratic Party Deputy Chief of Staff for Parliamentary Affairs Jeon Yong-ki also said on KBS Radio that day, "I hope (the push for a special counsel) is seen from the perspective of correcting wrongful content." He further stated, "Isn't it rather unreasonable for the Ministry of Justice to decide on dismissing or maintaining charges?" and argued, "It is appropriate for a neutral special counsel to determine matters related to maintaining charges," reiterating the same stance as the president. <<> The People Power Party objected, saying, "This shows a will to tamper with the judicial system even after the local elections sent a warning message through public sentiment." People Power Party Senior Spokesperson Park Seong-hoon stated, "It is a declaration to use power to erase one's own legal risks. Claiming that a special counsel nominated by the Democratic Party and appointed by the president is 'neutral' is a sophistry." (더불어민주당은 9일 이재명 대통령 사건을 공소 취소할 수 있는 ‘조작기소 특검’ 추진과 관련해 “잘못된 표적 수사를 바로잡겠다는 것”이라고 했다. 이 대통령이 전날 공소 취소에 대해 “잘못한 게 있으면 바로잡으면 되는 것”이라고 하자 사실상 특검법을 재추진하겠다는 입장을 밝힌 것이다. 특검법은 민주당이 지방선거 전 밀어붙이려다가 반발에 부딪혀 보류했었다. 야당은 “셀프 면죄부”라며 반발했다.)

item.title: "Public Sentiment Sends Warning to Ruling Party Too, Loss of 2030 Generation More Painful… Internal Power Struggles with Pointed Fingers Unacceptable" (“민심은 여당에도 경고장, 2030 이탈 더 뼈아파… 삿대질 당권 싸움 안돼”)
item.description:
"Public Sentiment Sends Warning to Ruling Party Too, Loss of 2030 Generation More Painful… Internal Power Struggles with Pointed Fingers Unacceptable" (“민심은 여당에도 경고장, 2030 이탈 더 뼈아파… 삿대질 당권 싸움 안돼”)

Lee Gwang-jae, a lawmaker of the Democratic Party of Korea who won the by-election for the Gyeonggi Hanam-gap National Assembly seat held alongside the June 3 local elections, said in an interview with this newspaper on the 9th, "This was an election where the people gave power to the Lee Jae-myung administration but sent a warning to the Democratic Party." The Democratic Party won 12 out of 16 provincial and metropolitan mayor elections but failed to reclaim the Seoul mayoral post, receiving an assessment of "won but lost." The Democratic Party also lost the National Assembly by-elections in Gyeonggi Pyeongtaek-eul and Busan Buk-gu, both former Democratic Party strongholds. Despite leading significantly in opinion polls for Hanam-gap, Rep. Lee barely won by a margin of 1,385 votes. <<> Regarding this, Rep. Lee stated, "The party made a strategic blunder by pushing the 'insurrection judgment' narrative from the start of the election," adding, "In the end, the people gave us a harsh whipping to wake up and sent us a warning." He further said, "We should have shouted 'empower the working government' from the beginning." <<> Concerning the analysis that the votes of the 2030 generation shifted toward the People Power Party rather than the Democratic Party, Rep. Lee said, "It's the result of the ruling Democratic Party failing to respond to the desperate pleas of young people." He added, "The fact that the Democratic Party didn't receive enough support from the 2030 generation this time doesn't mean the youth have become conservative. In the future, if we fail to resolve issues of good jobs and housing, no political party can guarantee its future." <<> He also directed sharp criticism at party members who, even after receiving the election results, have already begun full-scale internal power struggles ahead of the August party leadership election. With current leader Jeong Cheong-rae expected to seek re-election, contenders like Prime Minister Kim Min-seok and Rep. Song Young-gil are being mentioned as competitors. Rep. Lee stated, "While competition is necessary, we must not become overly mired in a power struggle. We should focus our party's energy on how to improve the people's livelihoods and quality of life." <<> Entering politics in 1988 as an aide to the late President Roh Moo-hyun during his time as a National Assembly member, Rep. Lee was a core member of the pro-Roh faction, often called "Roh's right-hand man." He served as Governor of Gangwon Province and has now become a four-term lawmaker with this election. <<> -How do you view the election results? <<> "A notable feature of this election is that, unlike past elections which involved straight-ticket voting for one party, people engaged in strategic cross-voting. The people empowered the Lee Jae-myung administration to work but sent a warning to the Democratic Party to do better and that the status quo is unacceptable. The Democratic Party was whipped. It was an election where support for the government and checks on it operated simultaneously." <<> -A landslide victory for the Democratic Party was expected, but you lost in Seoul, Daegu, and South Gyeongsang. <<> "It's the result of not sufficiently presenting solutions that resonate with voters' daily lives. Early in the election, the Democratic Party put forth 'insurrection judgment' while the People Power Party put forth 'dictatorship judgment.' Judgment on insurrection is important. But elections must ultimately address current life and the future. People wonder if tomorrow can be better than today." <<> -Are you saying that people's livelihoods should have been front and center? <<> "From the beginning, we should have put 'empower the working government' at the forefront and made the insurrection judgment a subtitle. Young generations move to Gyeonggi Province due to high Seoul housing prices, but their workplaces are in Seoul. They leave in the early morning, ride the hellish subway, and return home late at night. They worry about their children's education, childcare issues, and housing costs. The Democratic Party should have offered more concrete answers to these practical problems." <<> -What do you think was the reason for the defeat of Democratic Party Seoul mayoral candidate Jeong Won-o? <<> "From the start, I kept thinking, 'Can we really win this?' Candidate Jeong should have been more aggressive. As a challenger facing a four-term incumbent mayor, he needed to be bolder with policy pledges, but he wasn't. Examples include educational innovation to drastically reduce private English education costs, public education innovation using EBS, creating youth jobs using university sites, and new models combining childcare and housing policies. A message that would make Seoul citizens feel 'that's a fresh proposal' was needed, but the vision of what would improve if Jeong Won-o was elected seemed weak." <<> -There is also analysis that conservatives consolidated support due to the Democratic Party's push for a special counsel investigation into an alleged manipulated indictment. <<> "There is no disagreement that prosecution reform is necessary. As the National Assembly's special hearing on the alleged manipulated indictment progressed, there seemed to be consensus within the Democratic Party that the prosecution had overreached. However, whether that consensus should directly lead to 'dropping the charges' is a separate issue. I believe getting to the truth of the matter should take utmost priority." <<> -The exit polls from the three major broadcasters showed that the sentiment of the 2030 generation leaned towards the People Power Party. <<> "The Democratic Party has always been a party that stood with the younger generation. But failing to receive that support in this election, and in recent elections, is even more painful. We apologize to the 2030 generation. We reflect on this." <<> -What do you think is the reason? <<> "The Democratic Party became absorbed in factional infighting and power struggles, neglecting the 2030 generation who are struggling with job and housing issues. Some say the youth have become conservative, but that's an incorrect expression. It's a problem of our political world failing to respond to the desperate cries and pain in their lives." <<> -What is your position on incidents like the shortage of ballot papers? <<> "It is an extremely infuriating matter. The ruling and opposition parties must jointly mobilize everything, including a parliamentary investigation. The National Election Commission is not a sanctuary. Haven't there been numerous instances of personnel recruitment corruption, like employees using cronyism to hire relatives or acquaintances? Elections are the flower of democracy. If election management loses trust, the roots of democracy are shaken." <<> -The Democratic Party will elect its next party leader on August 17, and the competition for the party leadership is already fierce. <<> "We must not engage in divisive tactics or immerse ourselves in power struggles, pointing fingers at each other. There is too much blaming others for this election result. We must all take responsibility." <<> -What kind of leadership do you think should emerge? <<> "The next ruling party leadership should coordinate with the Lee Jae-myung administration, which is entering its second year. The goal of politics is to improve the quality of the people's lives. We must attend to issues like jobs, housing, childcare, education, medical benefits, and pensions. It cannot be approached abstractly. Hasn't President Lee Jae-myung nominated Han Sung-sook (former Naver executive) as the next Prime Minister and Minister of SMEs and Startups? He set a direction. It signifies that the nation must move towards a new economy, an innovative economy." <<> -There are also rumors that you, Rep. Lee Gwang-jae, might run for party leader. <<> "(Avoiding a direct answer, then replying upon being asked again) I will focus my efforts on ensuring the course of pragmatism prevails within the Democratic Party. (Laughter)" (6·3 지방선거와 함께 치러진 경기 하남갑 국회의원 보궐선거에서 당선된 더불어민주당 이광재 의원은 9일 본지 인터뷰에서 “국민이 이재명 정부에 힘은 실어주되 민주당에는 경고장을 보낸 선거였다”고 했다. 민주당은 시·도지사 선거 16곳 중 12곳은 이겼지만 서울시장 탈환에 실패하면서 “이겼지만 졌다”는 평가를 받고 있다. 민주당 지역구였던 경기 평택을, 부산 북갑 국회의원 재보선에서도 민주당은 졌다. 이 의원도 하남갑 여론조사에선 크게 앞섰지만 실제론 1385표차로 아슬아슬하게 이겼다.)

item.title: Lee: "How dare you insult someone who has joined our family?" – Aiming at division in Pyeongtaek B? (李 “우리 집안 온 사람 모욕하면 되겠느냐” 평택乙 분열 겨냥?)
item.description:
Lee: "How dare you insult someone who has joined our family?" – Aiming at division in Pyeongtaek B? (李 “우리 집안 온 사람 모욕하면 되겠느냐” 평택乙 분열 겨냥?)

President Lee Jae-myung's remarks during his first anniversary press conference on the 8th, where he said to the ruling party, "How dare you insult someone who has joined our family by saying, 'That's not our original color'?" have sparked a backlash. The comment came in response to a reporter's question about the local election results, and was interpreted as a jab at the leadership of Chung Cheong-rae, who failed to properly support Democratic Party candidate Kim Yong-nam in the Pyeongtaek B by-election. (이재명 대통령이 지난 8일 취임 1주년 기자회견에서 여권을 향해 “우리 집안에 들어온 사람한테 ‘원래 우리 색깔 아니야’ 모욕을 하면 되겠느냐”고 한 발언을 두고 후폭풍이 일고 있다. 이 발언은 지방선거 결과를 평가해 달라는 기자 질문에 답하면서 나왔는데, 경기 평택을 재선거에서 떨어진 민주당 김용남 후보를 제대로 돕지 않은 정청래 지도부를 저격한 발언으로 해석됐다.)

President Lee said on that day, "People who come inside the castle may have previously cursed us or may have different thoughts," adding, "Should we insult them by saying, 'You’ll eventually betray us and leave at any moment?'" He further stated, "The party in power and the party in opposition should naturally be different," and "The opposition must be adept at using a spear, but the ruling party must serve as a vessel." (이 대통령은 이날 “성 안으로 들어오는 사람들이 전에는 막 (우리를) 욕하던 사람일 수도 있고, 생각이 다른 사람일 수도 있다”며 “(그렇다고) ‘언제든지 나가서 배신할 거지?’라고 모욕을 하면 되겠느냐”고 했다. 그러면서 “집권했을 때의 당과 야당이었을 때의 당은 당연히 달라야 한다”며 “야당은 창을 잘 써야 하지만, 여당은 그릇이 돼야 한다”고 했다.)

Although President Lee did not specifically mention Pyeongtaek B, pro-Lee factions have remarked, "It’s about candidate Kim Yong-nam." Kim, a former Saenuri Party lawmaker, supported President Lee in the last presidential election and joined the Democratic Party. He was later persuaded by the Chung Cheong-rae leadership to run in Pyeongtaek B, originally a Democratic stronghold. During the election, he vied for the top spot with Cho Kuk of the Cho Kuk Innovation Party, but in the final tally, People Power Party candidate Yoo Eui-dong won. Even within the ruling party, the loss was analyzed as "the Democratic Party split into pro-Lee and pro-Moon factions, dividing support between Kim and Cho." In fact, pro-government YouTubers Kim Eo-joon and Yoo Si-min backed Cho. A pro-Lee insider commented, "Isn’t President Lee pointing out that the party leadership essentially stood by without addressing this situation?" <<> Within the Democratic Party’s support base, there are also divergent views on responsibility for the Pyeongtaek B by-election. Pro-Lee factions say, "It’s true that the party was hesitant to support Kim once various suspicions, such as his operation of a loan shark under a pseudonym, surfaced. That’s why we lost." However, hardline party members backing Representative Chung argue, "It’s also true that some local party members in Pyeongtaek left the party after Kim’s nomination," and "It was a candidate risk." (이 대통령이 평택을을 구체적으로 언급하지 않았지만 친명계에선 “김용남 후보 얘기”란 말이 나왔다. 새누리당 의원 출신인 김 후보는 지난 대선 때 이 대통령을 지지하며 민주당에 입당했다. 이후 김 후보는 정청래 지도부가 설득해 원래 민주당 지역구였던 평택을에 출마했다. 선거 과정에선 조국혁신당 조국 후보와 1·2위를 오가며 선두 경쟁을 펼쳤지만 개표 결과 국민의힘 유의동 후보가 당선됐다. 여권에서도 김 후보 패인에 대해 “민주당이 친명, 친문 둘로 쪼개져 김 후보, 조국 후보 쪽으로 갈라지면서 졌다”고 분석했다. 실제 친여 유튜버 김어준씨와 유시민씨 등은 조 후보를 밀었다. 친명계 인사는 “이런 상황을 정리하지 않고 사실상 방관한 여당 지도부를 이 대통령이 지적한 것 아니겠냐”고 했다.)

item.title: Jung Cheong-rae Excluded from Lee's Departure Event… Kim Min-seok Took His Place (李 출국 행사서 정청래 배제… 그 자리에 김민석 섰다)
item.description:
Jung Cheong-rae Excluded from Lee's Departure Event… Kim Min-seok Took His Place (李 출국 행사서 정청래 배제… 그 자리에 김민석 섰다)

On the 9th, when President Lee Jae-myung departed for a European tour to attend the G7 summit, Representative Jung Cheong-rae was absent from the airport farewell event. This was reportedly due to a request from the presidential office. Instead, Prime Minister Kim Min-seok, a candidate for party leadership, accompanied him on the trip. Amid deepening conflicts between the pro-Lee and pro-Jung factions ahead of the August party convention, various interpretations emerged within the Democratic Party regarding the scenes from the departure. <<> That morning at Seoul Air Base in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, attendees included Prime Minister Kim, Minister of the Interior and Safety Yoon Ho-jung, Presidential Chief of Staff Kang Hoon-sik, and Senior Political Secretary Hong Ik-pyo. Kim, who often appeared at return events rather than departures, smiled brightly, shook hands with President Lee, and waved at the departing plane. On site, Representative Jung and other Democratic Party leadership were entirely absent. This was the first time Jung skipped a presidential farewell event. Even amid party-government conflicts over disagreements on the prosecution reform plan, Jung had previously attended airport events. In response, the presidential office stated, "Considering the prolonged Middle East war and the poor management by the National Election Commission during the June 3 local elections, we minimized the number of farewell attendees." It was reported that Jung spent the day on an unofficial schedule, visiting Jeonju, North Jeolla Province, for a lunch meeting with governor-elect Lee Won-taek, a pro-Jung figure. <<> Some within the ruling bloc interpreted this as President Lee lending support to Prime Minister Kim, who has officially declared his bid for party leadership. A pro-Lee Democratic Party lawmaker said, "The president had already signaled 'next party leader = Kim Min-seok' by nominating the successor prime minister right after the election." In the party leadership election held in August last year, shortly after the Lee Jae-myung administration took office, Jung Cheong-rae, backed by party member support, defeated pro-Lee former lawmaker Park Chan-dae by a wide margin. At that time, the president remained neutral, saying, "The winning side is my side." A key ruling bloc insider noted, "But this time, the president is different. Since the next party leader will hold the nomination rights for the 2028 general election and the government is entering its second year, any discord between the party and government would be a big problem. He has no choice but to support Prime Minister Kim emotionally." Another Democratic Party lawmaker added, "At that time, President Lee probably regretted not explicitly supporting former lawmaker Park and ultimately losing party control. This time, he seems to want to send a clear signal to party members about who he supports." <<> Indeed, in a press conference the previous day, President Lee indirectly criticized the Jung Cheong-rae leadership regarding the June 3 local election results, saying "an incomprehensible situation occurred" and "being good at swearing doesn't make a strong party." In contrast, he praised Prime Minister Kim, saying, "I wonder if there's been a cabinet that produced so many concrete results in such a short time," and added, "Since it seems more appropriate for him to take on a different role, we decided to change roles." <<> Meanwhile, Jung is reportedly set to chair a Supreme Council meeting on the 10th and state his position on the election results. On the 12th, he plans to chair another Supreme Council meeting in Gwangju and visit the National May 18 Democratic Cemetery. Jung is expected to step down as party leader as early as this month and officially announce his bid for re-election. <<> Within the Democratic Party, disagreements are erupting over the "Jung Cheong-rae responsibility theory" regarding the election results. Lawmaker Im Mi-ae, chair of the party's North Gyeongsang Province chapter, wrote on Facebook the previous night, "The party leadership tried to ride on the president's approval ratings for the election, which was very negligent," adding, "From the perspective of Daegu and North Gyeongsang, it was a strategic failure." Pro-Lee lawmaker Kim Young-jin said in a radio interview that day, "In the early stages of the election, didn't the party leadership appear to be counting their chickens before they hatched?" Backlash also emerged against the "one-member-one-vote system for delegates and rights members," which Jung had pushed through. The next party leadership election will be the first to apply this system, with pro-Lee factions attacking it as "designed for Jung Cheong-rae, who has strong member support, to seek re-election." Regarding this, lawmaker Jeon Hyun-hee said, "It seems somewhat disconnected from general public sentiment," and added, "A complementary framework is needed." <<> On the other hand, Secretary-General Cho Seung-rae, close to Jung, said, "Whether this election constitutes a defeat severe enough for the party leader to resign—opinions seem divided on that." Pro-Jung lawmaker Choi Min-hee also urged, "Don't drag the president and presidential office into the party leadership primary and create a fake frame of pro-Lee versus pro-Jung." As factional conflicts escalate, some within the party expressed concerns that "excessive internal strife could provide a windfall for the opposition." (이재명 대통령이 G7(7국) 정상회의 참석차 유럽 순방길에 나선 9일 공항 환송 행사에 정청래 대표가 불참했다. 청와대 요청에 따른 것으로 알려졌다. 대신 이날 순방길에는 당권 주자인 김민석 국무총리가 함께했다. 8월 전당대회를 앞두고 친명과 친청 간 갈등의 골이 깊어지는 가운데 이날 순방길 장면을 두고 민주당에선 여러 해석이 나왔다.)

item.title: Distrust of In-Person Voting Spreads to Early Voting… Experts Say “Overall Voting System Needs Reassessment” (본투표 관리 불신, 사전투표로 번져… 전문가 “투표 제도 전반 재점검해야”)
item.description:
Distrust of In-Person Voting Spreads to Early Voting… Experts Say “Overall Voting System Needs Reassessment” (본투표 관리 불신, 사전투표로 번져… 전문가 “투표 제도 전반 재점검해야”)

The ‘ballot shortage crisis’ began when the National Election Commission (NEC) printed fewer in-person voting ballots than in the local elections four years ago. As early voting turnout increased with each election, the NEC printed only ‘over 50%’ of eligible voters’ worth of ballots for in-person voting, down from the previous ‘over 60%’—a prediction that proved wrong. Additionally, depending on the region or voters’ political leanings, there is a tendency to distrust early voting and opt for in-person voting, complicating election management. Some even say, “If this is how they manage in-person voting, how can we trust early voting?” Experts argue, “This crisis should be used as an opportunity to improve not only in-person voting but also early voting-related systems to resolve distrust.” <<> South Korea legalized early voting by amending the Public Official Election Act in 2012. The aim was to expand opportunities for citizens to exercise their suffrage and boost voter turnout. For national elections, it was first fully implemented in the June 2014 local elections. Early voting turnout has steadily risen from 11.49% in the 2014 local elections to 23.51% this year. <<> However, over the past few years, incidents such as ‘basket voting’ and ‘ballot paper removal from polling stations’ have sparked controversy over poor management of early voting. In response, the NEC installed surveillance cameras at locations where early voting ballot boxes were stored for monitoring in this local election and changed the ballot box stands to transparent ones. <<> The causes of distrust in early voting are identified as the ‘storage of early voting ballot boxes before counting’ and ‘transportation to the counting hall.’ Early voting takes place over two days—Friday and Saturday, five days before the main voting day. The early voting ballot boxes are then stored until the main voting day. The ‘difference in candidate vote shares between early voting and in-person voting’ has also been a persistent source of controversy. It is a culmination of issues the NEC brought upon itself, leading to distrust. <<> Among academics and experts, there is also a proposal to expand in-person voting. The idea is to combine early voting and in-person voting into a single 2-3 day voting period without any gap in dates. This would eliminate the very controversy over the storage of early voting ballot boxes. <<> Moon Sang-bu, a former member of the National Election Commission, stated, “It would work by allowing in-person voting for two days that also enables out-of-district voting, as with early voting. This would reduce opportunities for voters to participate in elections while addressing distrust in elections.” Shin Yul, a professor at Myongji University, also said, “The urgent matter is restoring trust in the elections themselves. We should consider a plan to conduct in-person voting over 2-3 days.” <<> They also noted the need to improve vote-counting methods. Former NEC member Moon Sang-bu added, “Ballot boxes from the first day should be kept directly in the counting hall, guarded by observers and police. When the two-day voting ends, ballots—including out-of-district ones—from that area should be counted locally.” The aim is to preempt any disputes over ballot transportation. <<> For example, if a person residing in Busan votes for Candidate A for Busan mayor in Jongno-gu, Seoul, their ballot should be counted in Jongno-gu rather than being transported to Busan, as is currently done. A political source commented, “Even in this case, a system to strictly monitor vote tallying would be necessary.” <<> There are also opinions to retain the current early voting and in-person voting systems but to completely overhaul the NEC, which manages elections, and deploy a large number of voting and counting personnel. Professor Um Ki-hong of Kyungpook National University and Professor Yoo Sung-jin of Ewha Womans University argued, “To improve early voting, we need to allocate more voting and counting personnel and budgets, and the NEC must tighten its management.” The 2022 local elections’ early voting involved a budget of 67 billion won and 110,000 personnel. <<> However, if the early voting system is maintained, there are suggestions to address the curiosity about the difference in vote shares between ruling and opposition candidates in early versus in-person voting—one of the bases for distrust. A pattern has consistently emerged where, in early voting, Democratic Party candidates often have higher vote shares, while in in-person voting, People Power Party candidates tend to catch up. There is also a growing trend of different participation rates in early and in-person voting among party supporter bases. <<> Kim Hyung-joon, a chair professor at Pai Chai University, said, “There is a need to verify why this phenomenon occurs, but the NEC has avoided it, further fueling claims of electoral fraud.” He added, “If the NEC had selected a few electoral districts as samples and had them verified by neutral bodies, then disclosed the results to the public, distrust in early voting could have been alleviated.” (‘투표용지 부족 사태’는 선거관리위원회가 본투표용지를 4년 전 지방선거 때보다 적게 인쇄하면서 시작됐다. 선거 때마다 사전투표율이 오르자 ‘유권자 수 60% 이상’을 인쇄했던 본투표용지를 ’50% 이상’만 인쇄했는데, 예측이 빗나간 것이다. 여기에 지역이나 유권자의 정치 성향에 따라 사전투표를 불신하고 본투표를 하려는 경향도 있어 투표 관리가 어려워진 측면도 있다. 일각에선 “본투표도 이렇게 관리하는데 사전투표는 어떻게 믿을 수 있겠느냐”는 얘기까지 나온다. 전문가들은 “이번 사태를 본투표뿐 아니라 사전투표 관련 제도를 개선해 불신을 해소하는 기회로 삼아야 한다”고 했다.)

item.title: 78% of Voters Said "Must Vote"... Yet 34 Regional Election Commissions Printed Only 50% of Ballots (“꼭 투표” 유권자 78% 였는데… 지역선관위 34곳, 용지 50%만 찍어)
item.description:
78% of Voters Said "Must Vote"... Yet 34 Regional Election Commissions Printed Only 50% of Ballots (“꼭 투표” 유권자 78% 였는데… 지역선관위 34곳, 용지 50%만 찍어)

As it emerged that the 255 district, city, and county election commissions nationwide printed ballots at widely varying rates, criticism arose in political circles that "election management was conducted without any standard." The National Election Commission (NEC) issued a guideline four years ago for the local elections to print at least 60% of the number of eligible voters for main election ballots, but this time it required at least 50%. This appears to reflect an expectation that the number of main election voters would decrease in line with the increasing trend of early voting. The NEC left the final decision on ballot printing to each local election commission, but subsequently failed to comprehensively manage the "disorderly ballot printing" by these local commissions, leading to an unprecedented situation where 91 polling stations ran out of ballots. In some areas with ballot shortages, prompt responses were also lacking. <<> According to the "Report on the Status of Ballot Shortages by the Election Commission" obtained by People Power Party lawmaker Kim Seung-soo on the 9th, the 255 district, city, and county commissions reportedly decided on the printing ratio for main election ballots by considering factors such as the early voting rate and overall turnout in recent elections. Early voting ballots are printed on-site, while main election ballots are pre-printed. <<> Breaking down the district, city, and county commissions, 34 of them decided to print ballots at the lower limit of 50% of the number of eligible voters. Fifteen commissions printed between over 50% and 55% or less, 82 printed between over 55% and 60% or less, and 101 printed between over 60% and 65% or less. Relatively few commissions prepared ballots generously: 16 printed between over 65% and 70% or less, 5 printed between over 70% and 75% or less, and 2 printed between over 75% and 80% or less. No commission printed ballots at a rate between over 80% and less than 100%. Only Incheon's Ongjin County, classified as a border area and special region, printed 100% of ballots matching the number of voters. <<> In particular, the Songpa District Election Commission in Seoul decided to print ballots at the lower limit of 50% for 25 of its neighborhoods, except for Jamsil 3-dong and Jamsil 4-dong (60%). For the district overall, this was at a 51% level. Contrary to the Songpa District Commission's predictions, the voter turnout in Songpa District this time was 65.8%, the fourth highest in Seoul. Consequently, 20 polling stations in Songpa District experienced ballot shortages. The commission stated, "The Songpa District Commission failed to consider the polling station-specific turnout from past elections." <<> As of the 9th, it was tallied that a total of 7,194 ballots were lacking nationwide in this election. The polling station with the most severe shortage was the 7th polling station in Jamsil 4-dong, Songpa District, Seoul, which lacked 436 ballots. This was followed by the 4th polling station in Cheongdam-dong, Gangnam District, Seoul (383 ballots), and the 4th polling station in Ganseok 1-dong, Namdong District, Incheon (306 ballots). <<> The location where voting was suspended for the longest time was the 2nd polling station in Jamsil 2-dong, Songpa District, Seoul. Voting was halted there for 105 minutes. This was followed by the 3rd polling station in Garak 2-dong, Songpa District, Seoul (97 minutes), the 5th polling station in Jamsil 2-dong, Songpa District, Seoul (95 minutes), and the 1st polling station in Munjeong 2-dong, Songpa District, Seoul (76 minutes). There are also testimonies that some voters gave up and left without voting, separate from the commission's situation assessment. <<> Ahead of this local election, the NEC proposed a lower limit of 50% of the number of voters as the ballot printing ratio. This was reportedly to consider "allegations of election fraud arising from leftover ballots" and "difficulties in printing, inspection, and storage." <<> The specific ballot printing ratio was decided separately by the 255 district, city, and county commissions, and it is understood that the NEC failed to properly verify these decisions. Local election commissions at the city/province, district/county, and town/neighborhood levels are composed of party nominees, judges, educators, etc., with the local chief judge usually elected as chairperson. A political source said, "The printing ratio was determined in a rough-and-ready manner based on just a few figures, such as the early voting rate and past turnout trends." Regarding the widespread delays in voting due to ballot shortages, there were also criticisms that "the election commission's response capability in emergency situations is also problematic." <<> In a survey conducted by the commission before this local election, the intention to actively participate in voting was 78.1%. Lawmaker Kim Seung-soo stated, "The ballot shortage incident clearly reveals the structural problems the election commission faces and means an accident could happen at any time," adding, "Fundamental consideration of the election commission's system and operation methods is necessary." (전국 255개 구·시·군 선거관리위원회가 인쇄한 투표용지 비율이 제각각인 것으로 드러나면서 정치권에서는 “선거 관리가 기준도 없이 이뤄졌다”는 비판이 제기됐다. 중앙선관위는 4년 전 지방선거 때는 본투표 용지를 유권자의 60% 이상 찍으라는 지침을 내렸지만 이번엔 50% 이상 인쇄하도록 했다. 사전투표 증가 추세에 맞춰 본투표 유권자가 줄어들 것이라 예상한 것으로 보인다. 중앙선관위는 투표용지 인쇄 최종 결정은 각 지역 선관위에 맡기는데, 이후 각 지역 선관위의 ‘중구난방 용지 인쇄’를 종합 관리하지 못했고, 91개 투표소에서는 투표용지가 모자라는 초유의 사태가 발생했다. 투표용지가 부족한 일부 지역에선 신속한 대처도 이뤄지지 못했다.)

item.title: Chang says "should hold national re-election" while within party "water down resignation talk" (張 “전국 재선거해야” 당내 “사퇴론 물타기”)
item.description:
Chang says "should hold national re-election" while within party "water down resignation talk" (張 “전국 재선거해야” 당내 “사퇴론 물타기”)

People Power Party leader Chang Dong-hyuk stated on the 9th regarding the shortage of ballot papers during the June 3 local elections, "I believe the local elections should essentially be held again," arguing for a nationwide re-election. Within the party, criticism emerged such as "an intention to water down the talk of the party leader's resignation" and "riding on the conspiracy theory of election fraud." (국민의힘 장동혁 대표가 9일 6·3 지방선거에서 발생한 투표용지 부족 사태와 관련해 “지방선거를 사실상 다시 실시해야 한다고 생각한다”며 전국 단위의 재선거를 주장했다. 당내에선 “당 대표 사퇴론에 물타기 하려는 의도” “부정선거 음모론에 올라타는 것”이라는 지적이 나왔다.)

Leader Chang held a press conference at the National Assembly that morning and said, "The fundamental solution to this incident of disenfranchisement is ultimately a nationwide re-election," adding, "I will promptly initiate internal party discussions to propose a special law for an immediate nationwide re-election." (장 대표는 이날 오전 국회에서 기자회견을 열고 “이번 참정권 박탈 사태를 근본적으로 해결하는 것은 결국 전국 재선거밖에 없다”며 “즉각 전국 재선거 실시를 위한 특별법을 발의할 수 있도록 신속하게 당내 논의를 진행하겠다”고 말했다.)

When asked whether his call for a re-election was a demand for the resignation of People Power Party-affiliated Seoul Mayor-elect Oh Se-hoon, Leader Chang did not give a clear stance. He said, "When discussing the principle of upholding liberal democracy, singling out a specific candidate and asking if it's pressure for that candidate's resignation is inappropriate, I believe." (장 대표는 재선거 주장이 국민의힘 소속 오세훈 서울시장 당선인의 사퇴를 요구하는 것이냐는 질문에는 명확하게 입장을 밝히지 않았다. 그는 “자유민주주의를 지키는 원칙을 얘기하는 데 있어 특정 후보 한 명만 거론하며 그게 특정 후보 사퇴 압박이냐고 묻는 건 온당치 않다고 생각한다”고 말했다.)

Voices within and outside the party have emerged to put the brakes on Leader Chang's re-election claim. Lawmakers Kim Do-eup, Jeong Jeom-sik, and Seong Il-jong (in order of preference), who are running for the People Power Party floor leader election, attended a private discussion meeting held in Yeouido that afternoon and drew a line against the re-election argument, saying, "A special counsel and a parliamentary investigation are the priority for now." (당 안팎에선 장 대표의 재선거 주장에 제동을 거는 목소리가 나왔다. 국민의힘 원내대표 선거에 출마한 김도읍·정점식·성일종 의원(기호순)은 이날 오후 여의도에서 열린 비공개 토론회에 참석해 “지금은 특검과 국정조사가 우선”이라며 재선거 주장과는 선을 그었다.)

Mayor-elect Oh Se-hoon said in a media interview regarding Leader Chang's claim, "I see it as a political slogan," adding, "The margin is over about 60,000 votes, so realistically, it is true that it's somewhat difficult to have an impact (as stipulated by the election law)." (오세훈 당선인은 언론 인터뷰에서 장 대표 주장과 관련해 “정치적 구호라고 생각한다”며 “격차가 한 6만표 이상 벌어져 현실적으로는 (선거법이 규정하는) 영향을 미치기가 좀 어려운 구조인 것은 사실”이라고 했다.)

item.title: Opposition Party Proposes Election Commission Special Counsel Bill as Party Policy… Ruling Party Avoids Direct Answer, Saying “We Will Discuss” (野, 선관위 특검법 당론 발의… 與는 “협의하겠다” 즉답 피해)
item.description:
Opposition Party Proposes Election Commission Special Counsel Bill as Party Policy… Ruling Party Avoids Direct Answer, Saying “We Will Discuss” (野, 선관위 특검법 당론 발의… 與는 “협의하겠다” 즉답 피해)

The People Power Party (PPP) on the 9th proposed a "Comprehensive Special Counsel Bill for the National Election Commission" as party policy to investigate suspicions related to the shortage of ballot papers during the June 3 local elections. The PPP maintains that a special counsel must be introduced to probe the relevant allegations. In contrast, the Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) expressed sympathy for the necessity of pursuing a special counsel but avoided giving a direct answer regarding the timing of its introduction. (국민의힘은 9일 6·3 지방선거 투표용지 부족 사태 관련 의혹을 수사하기 위한 ‘선관위 종합 특별검사법’을 당론으로 발의했다. 국민의힘은 관련 의혹 규명을 위해 특검을 도입해야 한다는 입장이다. 반면 더불어민주당은 특검 추진 필요성에 공감한다면서도, 도입 시기 등에 대해선 즉답을 피하고 있다.)

The PPP excluded the ruling party's right to recommend a special counsel in the bill proposed that day. Lawmaker Joo Jin-woo said on the same day, "If the DPK becomes the subject of special counsel recommendations, it would ultimately result in President Lee Jae-myung appointing the special counsel once again," adding, "Since the investigation must fundamentally be independent from power, we excluded the DPK's right to recommend a special counsel." (국민의힘은 이날 발의한 특검법에서 여당의 특검 추천권을 배제했다. 주진우 의원은 이날 “민주당이 특검 추천 대상이 되면 결국 이재명 대통령이 또다시 특검을 임명하는 상황이 된다”며 “기본적으로 권력으로부터 독립해 수사해야 하기 때문에 민주당의 특검 추천권을 배제했다”고 했다.)

The scope of the special counsel investigation includes not only the ballot paper shortage during the June 3 local elections and suspicions of attempts to cover it up, as well as illegal acts in the process of transporting ballot boxes with the mobilization of police force, but also suspicions that some candidates received identical vote counts during early voting. The total size of the special counsel team is set at 251 personnel, with a maximum investigation period of 170 days. This is the same scale as the second comprehensive special counsel law, which was the largest ever. (특검 수사 대상에는 6·3 지방선거 당시 투표용지 부족 사태와 이를 은폐하려 한 의혹, 경찰 공권력이 동원된 투표함 이송 과정의 불법행위뿐 아니라 사전 투표 과정에서 일부 후보들의 득표수가 같게 나온 의혹 등이 모두 포함됐다. 특검 전체 규모는 251명, 수사 기간은 최장 170일로 정했다. 이는 역대 최대 규모인 2차 종합 특검법과 동일한 규모다.)

In contrast, the DPK stated, "We are also open to discussing a special counsel (Han Jeong-ae, chair of the policy committee)," but is placing greater emphasis on a parliamentary investigation first. DPK floor leader Han Byung-do said on the 9th, "We will immediately convene a plenary session this week to report the parliamentary investigation plan," adding, "We will hold a vote directly at next week's plenary session to activate the special committee as quickly as possible." (반면 민주당은 “특검 역시 열어 놓고 협의할 것(한정애 정책위의장)”이라면서도, 우선 국정조사에 무게를 두고 있다. 한병도 민주당 원내대표는 9일 “이번 주 즉각 본회의를 개최해 국정조사 계획서를 보고하겠다”며 “다음 주 본회의에서 곧장 의결해 최단기간 내 특위를 가동하겠다”고 했다.)

Within the DPK, lawmaker Baek Hye-ryun proposed a special counsel bill on the 8th in her personal capacity. This bill stipulates that the DPK, the PPP, and the Rebuilding Korea Party each recommend one candidate for special counsel, and the president then appoints one of them. A key DPK official said, "If a special counsel is launched, Lawmaker Baek's special counsel bill will serve as the foundation," adding, "Especially, the ruling party's recommendation right must naturally be included." This special counsel bill targets seven incidents for investigation, including the calculation of ballot paper print quantities for the June 3 local elections and the decision-making process for election preparation. However, suspicions regarding identical vote counts in early voting, excessive use of police force, and illegal removal of ballot boxes are not included in the investigation scope. The investigation period is set at a maximum of 120 days, with a maximum investigative team size of 105 personnel. (민주당에선 백혜련 의원이 지난 8일 개인 자격으로 특검법을 발의했다. 이 법안은 민주당과 국민의힘, 조국혁신당이 각각 1명씩 특검 후보를 추천하면 대통령이 그중 한 명을 임명하도록 했다. 민주당 핵심 관계자는 “만약 특검을 하게 되면 백 의원 특검법이 기초가 될 것”이라며 “특히 여당 추천권은 당연히 포함해야 한다”고 했다. 이 특검법은 6·3 지방선거 투표용지 인쇄 물량 산정 및 투표 준비 의사결정 과정 등 7개 사건을 수사 대상으로 한다. 다만 사전투표 동일 득표수 의혹, 경찰의 과도한 공권력 행사와 투표함 불법 반출 의혹 등은 수사 대상에 포함되지 않았다. 수사 기간은 최장 120일이고, 수사 인력 규모는 최대 105명이다.)

The ruling and opposition parties are expected to begin full-fledged negotiations on the special counsel and parliamentary investigation after the PPP's new floor leader is elected on the 10th. (여야는 10일 국민의힘 새 원내대표가 선출된 이후 특검과 국정조사 등에 관해 본격적인 협상에 나설 전망이다.)

item.title: Songpa 51%, Ongjin 100%… A 'Jelly Salesman Ballot Paper' (송파 51%, 옹진은 100%… ‘엿장수 투표용지’)
item.description:
Songpa 51%, Ongjin 100%… A 'Jelly Salesman Ballot Paper' (송파 51%, 옹진은 100%… ‘엿장수 투표용지’)

On the main voting day of the June 3 local elections, the Ongjin County Election Commission in Incheon prepared ballot papers equal to the number of voters (100%). In contrast, in Seoul's Songpa District, only 51% of the number of voters' worth of ballot papers were printed. This discrepancy arose because 255 district, city, and county election commissions across the country each determined their own printing quantities based on past statistics and other factors. (6·3 지방선거 본투표 당일, 인천 옹진군 선거관리위원회는 유권자 수만큼(100%) 투표용지를 준비했다. 반면 서울 송파구에선 유권자 수의 51%만큼만 투표용지가 인쇄돼 있었다. 이런 차이는 전국 255개 구·시·군 선관위가 과거 통계 등을 근거로 제각각 투표용지 인쇄량을 정하면서 생겼다.)

This shortage of ballot papers began in many areas due to miscalculations by election commissions. At least 91 polling stations experienced a shortage of ballot papers, and even the additional supply of ballot papers was delayed, causing voting to be suspended for up to 1 hour and 35 minutes at 26 polling stations, including Seoul's Songpa District. Some people gave up on voting and turned away, which has escalated into demands for a re-election. (이번 투표용지 부족 사태는 상당수 지역에서 선관위 예측이 빗나가며 시작됐다. 최소 91곳 투표소에서 투표용지가 부족했고, 투표용지 추가 투입마저 늦어지면서 서울 송파구를 비롯해 26곳 투표소에서 최장 1시간 35분간 투표가 중단됐다. 투표를 포기하고 발길을 돌린 사람까지 생기면서 재선거 요구로까지 번졌다.)

According to the 'Report on the Ballot Paper Shortage' submitted by the National Election Commission to People Power Party lawmaker Kim Seung-soo on the 9th, the number of ballot papers prepared on the main voting day of the local elections varied by region. In Gwangju and Sejong, 50% of the number of voters' worth of ballot papers were printed, while in Gangwon, 66% were printed. Even within the same Seoul metropolitan area, Seoul and Gyeonggi printed 58%, and Incheon printed 53%. (9일 중앙선관위가 국민의힘 김승수 의원에게 제출한 ‘투표용지 부족 실태 보고서’(보고서)에 따르면, 지방선거 본투표 당일 준비된 투표용지는 지역마다 차이가 있었다. 광주, 세종에선 유권자 대비 50% 투표용지를 인쇄한 반면 강원은 66%를 인쇄했다. 같은 수도권에도 서울과 경기는 58%, 인천은 53%였다.)

Early voting, which allows voting anywhere in the country regardless of the electoral district, involves printing ballot papers at the polling station. In contrast, for the main voting on election day, ballot papers are pre-printed based on the number of voters and stored at the election commission. In December of last year, the National Election Commission sent a directive to district, city, and county election commissions stating, "If there is a need to reduce the print quantity, set the lower limit at 50% of the number of electors and adjust through individual committee resolutions." During the 2022 local elections, at least 60% or more of voters were to be printed, but as the number of early voters increased, the printing of main voting ballot papers was left to each election commission within the range of at least 50% of voters. The National Election Commission stated in the report that "some election commissions calculated the ballot paper printing ratio (relative to voters) without properly considering past polling station turnout rates." (지역구와 관계없이 전국 어디서든 투표할 수 있는 사전투표는 투표소에서 투표용지를 출력한다. 반면 선거 당일 본투표는 유권자 수를 감안해 미리 투표지를 인쇄해 선관위에 보관한다. 중앙선관위는 작년 12월 구·시·군 선관위에 “(투표용지) 축소 인쇄 필요성이 있을 경우 선거인 수 50% 하한선으로 잡고 개별 위원회 의결로 조정하라”는 지침을 보냈다. 2022년 지방선거 때는 최소 유권자의 60% 이상을 인쇄하도록 했지만 사전투표하는 사람이 늘면서 본투표용지 인쇄는 유권자 50% 이상 범위에서 각 선관위에 맡긴 것이다. 중앙선관위는 보고서에서 “일부 선관위에서 과거 투표소별 투표율 등을 제대로 고려하지 않고 (유권자 대비) 투표용지 인쇄 비율을 산정했다”고 했다.)

On the 9th, the Supreme Prosecutors' Office announced the establishment of a joint prosecution and police investigation headquarters (led by Deputy Chief Prosecutor Kim Tae-hoon) at the Seoul Central District Prosecutors' Office to uncover the truth behind the ballot paper shortage incident. The Seoul Eastern District Court partially granted the request for evidence preservation filed by the Reform Party, including for ballot paper storage boxes, security camera footage, and records of group chat rooms of election commission staff at some polling stations in Seoul's Songpa District. Student councils from 12 universities nationwide plan to issue a statement of national affairs on the 10th to denounce the ballot paper shortage incident. (대검은 9일 서울중앙지검에 투표용지 부족 사태 진상 규명을 위한 검경 합동수사본부(본부장 김태훈 3차장)를 설치한다고 밝혔다. 서울동부지법은 개혁신당이 낸 서울 송파구 일부 투표소의 투표용지 보관상자, 방범카메라 영상, 선관위 직원 단체대화방 기록 등에 대한 증거보전 신청을 일부 인용했다. 전국 12개 대학교 총학생회는 10일 투표용지 부족 사태를 규탄하는 취지의 시국선언에 나설 예정이다.)

item.title: “Do I Still Look Like a ‘Yoon Who Doesn’t Drink, a Lee with Decency’?” (“아직도 제가 ‘술 안 먹는 尹, 싸가지 있는 李로 보이나요?”)
item.description:
I found myself laughing alone while watching the TV debate for the Busan Buk-gu Gap by-election. When Democratic Party candidate Ha Jung-woo scolded independent candidate Han Dong-hoon, saying, “Shouldn’t you take moral responsibility and control the nuisance your fandom is causing?” Han Dong-hoon fired back in his characteristic tone. (부산 북구갑 재보선 TV 토론을 보다 혼자 웃었습니다. 더불어민주당 후보 하정우가 무소속 후보 한동훈을 향해 “(당신) 팬덤이 민폐 끼치는 것에 도의적 책임을 지고 통제해야 하는 것 아닙니까?” 하고 나무라자, 한동훈이 특유의 어투로 받아칩니다.)

“Isn’t it pretty ‘jjak-chi’ for a politician from a ruling party to tell an independent politician and say, ‘I have no supporters, so don’t let your supporters come either’?” (“거대 여당에서 나온 정치인이, 무소속 정치인한테, 나는 지지자 없으니, 너네 지지자도 오지 말라고 하는 건, 되게 ‘짜치는’ 일 아닌가요?”)

‘Jjak-chida’ is reportedly a Gyeongsang Province dialect meaning ‘to be hard up’ or ‘to be in a tough spot.’ It’s recently become trendy among young people on social media, turning into slang that sarcastically describes ‘a situation that falls short of expectations or looks shabby.’ I first heard this novel word two years ago when I interviewed Han Dong-hoon, then the People Power Party leader. (‘짜치다’는 ‘쪼들리다’ ‘형편이 어렵다’는 뜻의 경상도 방언이라고 합니다. 최근 소셜미디어를 타고 젊은이들 사이 유행하면서 ‘기대에 못 미치거나 없어 보이는 상황’을 비꼬는 속어가 됐다는데, 저는 이 신박한 단어를 2년 전 한동훈 당시 국민의힘 대표를 인터뷰하다 처음 들었습니다.)

It was when I asked him if he was bothered by the widening gap with Lee Jae-myung in Gallup polls on presidential suitability. (당신 대선 적합도를 묻는 갤럽 조사에서 이재명과의 격차가 점점 벌어지는 것이 신경 쓰이지 않느냐고 물었을 때지요.)

“Do weekly ups and downs really matter? Don’t I sometimes win? Do those things mean much? Isn’t it a bit jjak-chi for a party leader to even talk about response rates from opinion polls?” (“매주 오르내리는 수치가 중요한가요? 제가 이길 때도 있지 않나요? 그런 거가 큰 의미가 있나요? 당대표가 여론조사에서 나온 응답률, 그런 거에 대해서까지 얘기하는 건 좀 짜치지 않나요?”)

It’s not just ‘jjak-chida.’ From the moment we met at a cafe in Yeouido at 8 a.m. for the interview, party leader Han Dong-hoon was unfiltered. (‘짜치다’뿐이 아닙니다. 아침 8시, 인터뷰를 위해 여의도 카페에서 만난 순간부터 당대표 한동훈은 거침이 없었습니다.)

“The cafe is open (not a private room)—are you okay with that?” (“카페가 (룸이 아니라) 오픈돼 있는데 괜찮으시겠어요?”)

“I’m pretty shameless.” (“저, 뻔뻔한 편입니다.”)

“There are comments that you’ve changed a bit since becoming party leader?” (“당대표 되고 나서 좀 달라졌다는 평이 있던데요?”)

“I’m in a position where I have to say, ‘If the sun doesn’t rise, let’s go by the moon,’ so the responsibility feels heavier, but I don’t think I’ve changed. I’ve always lived life on my own terms.” (“해가 안 뜨면 달을 보고 가자고 해야 하는 자리이니 책임감은 커졌겠지만, 저 자신이 달라진 건 아닐 겁니다. 저는 늘 쪼대로 살아왔다고 생각합니다.”)

I also learned a ‘new vocabulary’ when he took aim at the Democratic Party’s introduction of the financial investment income tax. (민주당 금투세 도입을 저격하는 대목에서도 ‘새 어휘’를 배웠습니다.)

“A 1 vs. 99 split? Sorry, but 14 million individual investors know the market way better than Policy Chief Jin Seong-joon. When the Democratic Party uses a rich-versus-poor frame and says ‘This is a 1 vs. 99 issue,’ everyone will think, ‘They’re just nonsense.’” (“1대 99로 갈라치기? 미안하지만 진성준 정책의장보다 1400만 개미 투자자들이 시장을 훨씬 더 잘 알걸요? 민주당이 부자와 빈자를 나누는 프레임으로 ‘이건 1대 99의 문제’라고 하면, 다들 ‘까고 있네’ 이럴 겁니다.”)

Of course, he was equally blunt when asked about his conflict with President Yoon Suk Yeol. (물론 윤석열 대통령과의 갈등을 묻는 질문에도 얄짤없습니다.)

“It’s true we need to resolve the conflict, but we also have to do what’s right. I wouldn’t say, ‘It’s okay to take bribes?’ just for short-term gain. That would be embarrassing.” (“갈등을 해소해야 하는 건 맞지만, 옳은 일을 해야 하니까요. 순간의 유불리를 위해 ‘가방을 받는 건 괜찮다?’라고 말하진 않을 겁니다. 쪽팔리잖아요?”)

I was well aware of Han Dong-hoon’s tongue, said to have decimated the National Assembly with a 180-to-1 ratio, but I was taken aback by these bold, rebellious teenage words coming from a top-notch elite graduate of Seoul National University Law School and Columbia University. As soon as my question ended, answers poured out without a second’s hesitation, leaving even a 30-year veteran female journalist like me defenseless. When I asked why he was so good with words, he indirectly implied it was innate. (180대 1로 국회를 초토화시켰다는 한동훈의 말발은 익히 알고 있었지만 서울법대, 컬럼비아대 출신 초엘리트 입에서 10대 소년의 저돌적이고 반항적인 단어들이 튀어나오니 당황스럽더군요. 질문이 끝나기가 무섭게 1초의 머뭇거림도 없이 쏟아지는 답변엔 30년 아줌마 기자도 속수무책. ‘왜 그리 말을 잘하냐’ 물으니 ‘타고났다’는 말을 우회적으로 하더군요.)

“I’ve tried preparing my answers in advance, but it only got more tangled. So instead (of preparing responses), I’d rather get more sleep and just go in.” (“해야 말을 미리 준비해본 적도 있는데, 더 꼬이더라구요. 그래서 (답변을 준비하느니) 차라리 잠을 더 많이 자고 가자, 합니다.”)

Political analysts cite Han Dong-hoon’s strengths as outstanding linguistic ability and debate skills, but they also analyze that these could be weaknesses. In politics, the ability to include diverse groups and show empathy is just as important as logically overpowering opponents. That’s why many find Han Dong-hoon’s speaking style refreshing, but just as many perceive it as arrogant. If you break it down, everything he says is correct, but does it leave you feeling bad after hearing it? It’s like the grumbling of elders who say, “He just can’t let a single word slide”—probably because he gives the impression of trying to win rather than persuade. (정치 평론가들은 한동훈의 강점으로 탁월한 언어 능력과 토론 실력을 꼽지만 동시에 그것이 약점이 될 수 있다고 분석합니다. 정치에서는 상대를 논리로 제압하는 능력만큼이나 다양한 세력을 아우르는 포용력과 공감 능력도 중요하니까요. 한동훈 화법을 두고 시원하다는 사람도 많지만 건방지다고 느끼는 사람도 적지 않은 이유입니다. 뜯어보면 다 맞는 말인데 듣고 나면 기분이 나빠진다고 할까? ‘한마디를 안 져~’라는 어르신들 끌탕처럼 상대를 설득하기보다 이기려 한다는 인상을 주기 때문일 겁니다.)

But the more I interviewed him, the more I felt Han Dong-hoon was a different breed from the typical politicians we usually see. It’s like he doesn’t follow the grammar of established Korean politics. Regardless of whether he has decency, he seemed like a ‘political new species’ in his own right. (그런데 인터뷰를 할수록 한동훈은 우리가 흔히 보아온 정치인의 전형과는 다른 사람이란 생각이 들더군요. 기존 한국 정치의 문법을 따르지 않는다고 할까요? 싸가지 여부와는 다른, 그 자체로 ‘정치 신인류’ 같았습니다.)

For example, even after the People Power Party suffered a crushing defeat in the general election he led as emergency committee chair, Han Dong-hoon immediately challenged for party leadership. This is completely different from traditional politicians who take responsibility for defeat, go abroad for at least six months, and return after lying low. When I said during the interview, “Many elder politicians worry that your return was too quick and hasty,” Han Dong-hoon answered without taking a breath. (이를테면, 비대위원장으로 이끈 총선에서 국민의힘이 처절히 패배했는데도 한동훈은 곧바로 당권에 도전합니다. 기존 정치인들이 패배에 책임을 지고 해외로 나가 최소 6개월 공백기를 두고 은인자중하다 돌아오는 것과는 전혀 다른 모습이지요. 인터뷰 때도 제가 “너무 빠른 복귀, 성급함을 걱정하는 원로 정치인이 많다”고 하자, 한동훈이 숨도 안 쉬고 답하더군요.)

“Are they really, like, massively, worried about me? As for me, if something helps the country thrive right now, I’d probably just choose it without much thought.” (“그분들이 진짜, 저를, 막, 대단히, 걱정해 줘서 그러는 걸까요? 저는 지금 이 순간 나라가 잘되는 일에 도움이 되는 거라면, 별생각 없이 그거 선택할 것 같은데요?”)

Even after losing the presidential primary, Han Dong-hoon doesn’t disappear from the public eye. He showcases his resilience through the YouTube channel “I’m Han Dong-hoon,” continuously engaging with the public. (대선 경선 패배 후에도 한동훈은 국민의 시야에서 사라지지 않습니다. 유튜브 ‘한동훈입니다’를 통해 자신의 건재함을 보여주며 대중과 소통을 끊임없이 이어가지요.)

Perhaps because it’s an off-field campaign, the topics are diverse. Sitting on a sofa or driving in a car, he talks about trivial musical tastes—whether he likes Lim Yun-chan or Cho Seong-jin—favorite books, authors, food, and so on. It’s said he wore long hair and a gold necklace during his Seoul National University days, and in my interview with him, I recall he had plenty of ‘wild energy’ stories. (장외전이라 그런지 주제도 다양하더군요. 소파에 앉아서, 혹은 자동차를 타고 가면서 임윤찬을 좋아하는지, 조성진을 좋아하는지 같은 사사로운 음악적 취향, 좋아하는 책, 작가, 음식 이야기 등등. 서울대 시절 장발에 금목걸이를 하고 다녔다더니, 저와 인터뷰 때도 ‘똘끼’ 충만한 얘기를 했던 것 같습니다.)

Like liking Park Chan-wook’s flop film “I’m a Cyborg, But That’s OK,” being struck by the line “Abandon hope, but stay strong,” describing himself as a pessimistic optimist, saying he buys several books and spreads them on the floor reading one after another, or that he plays the guitar and sings with Netflix on… Could this genius yet rebellious nature, stubbornness, and restless diligence have been the engine that made Han Dong-hoon a living, breathing populist politician? (박찬욱 영화 중 폭망한 ‘싸이보그지만 괜찮아’를 좋아한다든가, 거기 나오는 ‘희망을 버려, 그래도 힘내’라는 대사에 꽂혔다든가, 자신은 비관적 낙관주의자라든가, 책을 사 오면 여러 권 방바닥에 펼쳐놓고 이거 읽었다 저거 읽었다 한다든가, 넷플릭스를 틀어놓고 기타를 치며 노래를 부른다든가 등등…. 이런 천재적 꼴통 기질과 고집, 잠시도 가만히 있지 않는 바지런함이 한동훈을 대중 정치인으로 살아 움직이게 한 엔진이었을까요?)

Elderly conservatives who disapprove of Han Dong-hoon often lament his “unbearable lightness.” “He’s smart, but too light” or “He’s arrogant!” Even I felt uncomfortable and intimidated by his fast, aggressive, and combative speaking style, but I haven’t given up on my expectations for him because of a few unforgettable scenes. (한동훈을 마땅찮아하는 보수의 어르신들은 종종 그의 ‘참을 수 없는 가벼움’을 토로합니다. “똑똑하긴 한데 너무 가벼워” 혹은 “건방져!” 빠르고 저돌적이고 공격적인 한동훈식 화법은 저조차도 불편하고 주눅 들었지만, 잊지 못할 몇 가지 장면이 있어 그에 대한 기대를 아직 접지 않았습니다.)

The first scene was when, as Minister of Justice, he met the mother of the late Private Hong Jeong-ki, who died of a cerebral hemorrhage during military service. When Hong’s mother pointed to the photo of her son in horn-rimmed glasses and said, “Minister, he looked like you. He was such an upright child,” tears burst from Han Dong-hoon, who seemed like he wouldn’t shed a drop even if pricked. Startled himself, he hastily wiped his tears with a tissue and held Hong’s mother’s hand, promising to quickly pass the State Compensation Act amendment. (첫 장면은 법무장관 시절, 군 복무 중 뇌출혈로 사망한 고(故) 홍정기 일병의 어머니를 만났을 때입니다. 홍 일병 어머니가 뿔테 안경을 쓴 영정 속 아들을 가리키며 “장관님과 우리 아들이 닮았다. 참 올곧은 아이였다”고 하자, 찔러도 피 한 방울 안 나올 것 같던 한동훈에게서 눈물이 터집니다. 자신도 놀랐는지 휴지로 허겁지겁 눈물을 닦으며 홍 일병 어머니의 손을 잡은 그는, 국가배상법 개정안을 신속히 통과시키겠노라 약속하더군요.)

The second scene was during the 2024 general election when, as emergency committee chair, he went to Busan to give a speech and then performed a deep bow to citizens. Unlike other lawmakers, Han Dong-hoon suddenly took off his shoes and bowed. I remember my mother-in-law, watching the news, saying proudly, “He knows how to bow—the young man understands etiquette.” (두 번째 장면은 2024년 총선 당시 비대위원장 자격으로 부산에 내려가 연설한 뒤 시민들에게 큰절을 할 때입니다. 다른 국회의원들과 달리 한동훈은 갑자기 구두를 벗더니 절을 하더군요. 함께 뉴스를 보던 시어머님이 “쟈는 절을 할 줄 아네, 젊은 애가 예법을 알아” 하시며 대견해하시던 기억이 납니다.)

The decisive scene was definitely the ‘mukbang’ at Busan’s Gupo Market. An elderly vegetable seller handed him sticky rice wrapped in a plastic bag, and he sat on the ground, piling on kimchi and chewing away. I hear even the 70-80 age group, who hated Han Dong-hoon as a ‘traitor,’ had their resentment melt away at that scene, right? He even held his inauguration ceremony modestly with residents, including the ‘sticky rice grandma,’ instead of surrounding himself with influential politicians like a backdrop. No matter how capable Han Dong-hoon is, winning in Busan, a place where he has no ties, especially in Buk-gu Gap, a Democratic Party stronghold, must have been uncertain. Yet he mingled freely with everyone from elementary school students to 30-40s moms and 80-90s elderly, literally sweeping the ground with his whole body. Even if it was a calculated strategy, could it have been any smarter? (결정적인 장면은 역시 부산 구포시장 ‘먹방’입니다. 시장에서 채소를 파는 할머니가 비닐봉지에 담아 건넨 찰밥을 땅바닥에 앉은 채로 김치를 얹어 우적우적 먹는 모습. 한동훈을 ‘배신자’라 증오해 온 7080 노년층도 그 장면에 그간의 미움이 녹아내렸다고 하지요? 개소식도 유력 정치인들을 병풍처럼 둘러세우지 않고 ‘찰밥 할머니’를 비롯한 주민들과 함께 소탈하게 치르더군요. 제아무리 한동훈이어도 연고 없는 부산, 그중에서도 민주당 텃밭인 북구 갑에서 승리를 장담할 순 없었을 텐데, 초등학생부터 3040 엄마들, 8090대 노인들까지 스스럼없이 어울리며 그야말로 바닥을 온몸으로 훑고 다니더군요. 의도된 전략이었다 해도 이보다 영리할 수 있을까요?)

Now that he’s finally entered the National Assembly, Han Dong-hoon is on a roll. His supporters are said to be buzzing with excitement, hoping he will not only develop the underdeveloped Busan Buk-gu Gap but also enter the Legislation and Judiciary Committee to ‘teach a lesson’ to the brainless political scene. (마침내 국회에 입성한 한동훈은 파죽지세입니다. 그의 지지자들은 낙후된 부산 북구 갑을 발전시키는 건 물론, 국회 법사위에 들어가 무뇌아적 정치의 현장을 ‘참교육’시켜 주리라는 기대로 잔뜩 들떠 있다는군요.)

Living life on his own terms, avoiding both jjak-chi and embarrassing actions—will Han Dong-hoon turn the National Assembly upside down with shocking moves and reversals? Can he shed the prosecutor’s habits that everyone worries about and evolve into a cool politician? Can he become a politician who listens to and embraces diverse opinions with the humility of saying, ‘I could be wrong’? Can he march all the way to the Blue House, as the Gupo Market grandma hoped? (쪼대로 살고, 짜치는 일, 쪽팔리는 일은 하지 않겠다는 한동훈은 어떤 파격과 반전으로 국회를 뒤집어 놓을까요? 모두가 우려하는 검사의 습성을 버리고 쿨한 정치인으로 진화할 수 있을까요? ‘내가 틀릴 수 있다’는 겸양으로 다양한 의견을 듣고 포용하는 정치인이 될 수 있을까요? 구포시장 할머니의 바람대로 청와대까지 진격할 수 있을까요?)

Or will he set aside all these expectations and become just another forgotten, mediocre politician enjoying the hundreds of privileges of a lawmaker? (아니면 이 모든 기대를 뒤로하고 그 또한 국회의원의 수백 가지 특권만 누리다 잊히는 지리멸렬한 정치인이 되고 말까요?)

During the interview two years ago, I asked Han Dong-hoon a cheeky question. (2년 전 인터뷰 때 한동훈에게 짓궂은 질문을 던졌습니다.)

“People say Han Dong-hoon is ‘a Yoon who doesn’t drink, a Lee with decency’—what do you think of that?” (“한동훈은 ‘술 안 먹는 윤석열, 싸가지 있는 이준석’이라고 하던데 어떻게 생각하세요?”)

A question that must have been highly unpleasant and uncomfortable, yet this man didn’t even blink as he answered. (매우 불쾌하고 불편한 질문일 텐데도 이 남자, 눈도 깜짝 않고 답하더군요.)

“If that (mockery) is right, I’ll survive; if it’s wrong, I’ll disappear. Let’s check back in about a year.” (“그 말(조롱)이 맞다면 계속 살아남을 거고, 틀리면 사라지겠죠. 한 1년 뒤에 보시죠.”)
